data.content_ref: inline:The stated standard (§11.3) is 'audit the critic: adjudication-ritual flags sustained'. The target's rationale—that cross-critic consistency across SRC_007 and SRC_009 'demonstrates an invariant self-consistency property'—substitutes a coherence-based justification for an adjudication standard. §11.3 requires showing the ritual flags were properly sustained (i.e., the adjudication correctly applied the flagging criteria to the substance under audit), but the target argues from the mere fact that multiple stances agree (consistency), not from a demonstration that the flagging rule was correctly triggered by the audited content. Under a falsificationist epistemic standard, cross-stance agreement is not evidence that the flags were correctly sustained; it is at best evidence of neighborhood convergence, which does not adjudicate whether any individual flag was properly applied. The target thus answers 'why do the stances agree?' rather than 'why are the ritual flags correctly sustained?'—failing the problem as stated.
